figures.caption: Figure 1: Primary near-eye site-average associations between VLSQ-8 and nine personal light-exposure metrics. Effects compare scores separated by one participant-level SD. The upper panel is an absolute difference in hours for time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep; the lower panel shows ratios and corresponding percentage changes for eight log-link outcomes. Horizontal bars are 95% Wald CIs; none of the nine associations retained FDR-adjusted support.

Figure 2: Complementary chest site-average associations between VLSQ-8 and nine personal light-exposure metrics. Effects compare scores separated by one participant-level SD. The hour-difference and ratio outcomes remain on separate scales; horizontal bars are 95% Wald CIs. None retained FDR-adjusted support.
Figure 3: Near-eye and chest VLSQ-8 associations on identical participant-day samples. The dashed diagonal marks equal point estimates and grey lines mark the null; it is not an equivalence analysis.
Figure 4: Selected primary near-eye model checks for all nine metrics. Panels retain their model-specific transformed or Pearson-residual scales and are diagnostic rather than effect displays.
Figure 5: Primary and gap-timing-unaware VLSQ-8 associations on identical participant-day samples, shown separately for near-eye and chest placements.
